method: Direct visual inspection of 10 decoded candidate frames and all 10 stored reference frames in contact sheets; comparison of typography, character scale, composition, staging and visible clipping. This is independent visual judgment, not an automated metric verdict.

findings.observation: Candidate uses small thin sans-serif word or phrase snippets near the top. Reference frames use large expressive bold two-line headlines. Candidate examples include Stop, Watch the, Why does, winning, and I’m.
findings.repair: Increase headline prominence and expressive typography while preserving caption readability and safe areas.

findings.observation: Candidate actors generally appear around 25–35% of frame height, with small faces. Reference actors frequently appear around 40–55% and make facial expressions easier to read. These proportions are visual estimates, not measured bounding boxes.
findings.repair: Add closer framing and larger visible expressions at emotionally important beats.

findings.observation: Candidate samples repeatedly center isolated figures and floating symbolic props in medium or wide composition. References include book, bed, couch and interpersonal staging with more varied scene context. Static samples do not establish the full camera trajectory.
findings.repair: Vary close, medium and wide staging and connect props to visible character actions and scene context.

findings.observation: Candidate background is white; references use beige paper. White is an explicit target style and must not be treated as a parity failure by itself.
No visible text or character clipping observed in the sampled frames. This does not certify unsampled frames.
Still reference frames and sampled candidate frames cannot establish motion parity, acting continuity, audio quality, or full pacing.

limitations: Stored reference-frame provenance and timestamps were not independently revalidated against source video in this review.
No retention or competitive performance claim.
Static comparisons are not temporally aligned scene equivalents.
